items.title: Share price and intrinsic value can diverge for years
items.claim: Robert Shiller's work (Nobel 2013) showed stock prices vary much more than fundamental dividends would justify. What's the implication for share price as a measure of company performance?

options.text: Share price always equals intrinsic value at all times
Share prices can diverge from intrinsic value for extended periods (excess volatility); managers focused on quarterly share prices may make worse long-term decisions
Share price has no link to fundamentals ever
Only private firms have intrinsic value

items.reveal_title: Markets price emotions as well as cash flows
items.reveal:
Shiller's 1981 American Economic Review paper showed S&P 500 prices fluctuated 5-13x more than dividend-based fair value would justify. Tech bubble peaks (2000, 2021) and crisis troughs (2009, 2020) bookend this excess volatility.

Warren Buffett quotes Benjamin Graham: 'In the short run the market is a voting machine, in the long run a weighing machine.' Managers paid largely in stock options can be incentivised to manage the voting machine rather than build long-term weight.
items.why: Headline share price moves often reflect investor sentiment as much as company performance. Compensation and strategy that anchor on share price import this volatility.

items.title: The 7Ps were extended for services, not because the 4Ps were wrong
items.claim: The original 4Ps (product, price, place, promotion) were proposed by E. Jerome McCarthy in 1960. Why were three more Ps added later?

options.text: Booms and Bitner (1981) added people, process and physical evidence to capture the special characteristics of service industries (intangibility, inseparability, variability, perishability)
Because digital marketing required four extra Ps

items.reveal:
Bernard Booms and Mary Bitner's 1981 chapter 'Marketing Strategies and Organization Structures for Service Firms' added People (staff interactions with customers), Process (service delivery procedures) and Physical evidence (the tangible elements customers see).

A haircut, a flight or a consultation can't be inventoried, tested or returned. The 4Ps work better for tangible goods than for services, which by 2020 made up around 80% of UK GDP.
items.why: Frameworks evolve as the economy does. The 7Ps reflect a shift toward services that has continued since 1981.

items.title: Profitable businesses fail when cash runs out
items.claim: A construction firm books £5 million revenue and £500,000 profit in 2023 but customers pay 120 days after invoicing while suppliers demand 30 days. What is the most likely outcome?

options.text: Strong cash position because of the reported profit
A cash flow gap large enough to threaten survival, despite profitability — overtrading
Profit and cash will be identical
Suppliers must accept 120-day payment by law

items.reveal:
Carillion, the UK construction giant, reported £147 million profit in 2016 and collapsed in January 2018 with £1.5 billion of debt. A large part of the gap between profit and cash came from long receivable cycles on government contracts combined with aggressive revenue recognition.

'Profit is opinion; cash is fact' is an accounting saying with an empirical basis. The UK Insolvency Service reports that 80%+ of business failures involve a cash-flow rather than profitability problem.
items.why: Reported profit can lead, lag or diverge from cash entirely. Working capital management is often what separates surviving and failing firms.
